tagline: China's imperial capital holds the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven and centuries-old hutong alleyways, with the Great Wall climbing the mountains just beyond the city. It is ranked #30 on Time Out's Best Cities 2026 list.
overview: Beijing has been China's capital for much of the last 700 years, and the Ming-era monuments still dominate. The Forbidden City, home to 24 emperors, is the largest palace complex on Earth, facing the vast expanse of Tiananmen Square.

The city's soul lives in its hutongs, the narrow lanes of courtyard homes radiating from the old centre. Around Houhai's lakes, rickshaws, teahouses and snack stalls keep the neighbourhood feel alive, while the 798 Art District and Sanlitun show Beijing's modern side.

The Great Wall is the day trip everyone comes for. The restored Mutianyu section, about 90 minutes away, winds over forested ridges with far fewer crowds than Badaling. Back in the city, order Peking duck, roasted to a crackle and wrapped in pancakes, a dish perfected for the imperial court.

funFacts.title: HOME TO 24 EMPERORS
funFacts.text: The Forbidden City was the imperial palace for the Ming and Qing dynasties from 1420 until 1912.

funFacts.title: THE GREAT WALL NEXT DOOR
funFacts.text: The Mutianyu section of the Great Wall lies in the mountains about 70 kilometres from the city centre.

funFacts.title: SEVEN UNESCO SITES
funFacts.text: Beijing has seven UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including the Forbidden City, Temple of Heaven and Summer Palace.

funFacts.title: FIRST DOUBLE OLYMPIC CITY
funFacts.text: Beijing is the first city to host both the Summer Olympics, in 2008, and the Winter Olympics, in 2022.

funFacts.title: A SQUARE FOR A MILLION
funFacts.text: Tiananmen Square is one of the largest public squares in the world, built to hold a million people.

funFacts.title: ANCIENT ALLEYWAYS
funFacts.text: Some hutong lanes date back more than 700 years, though many have been lost to redevelopment.

funFacts.title: PEKING DUCK

funFacts.title: 3,000 YEARS OLD
funFacts.text: A settlement has stood on this site for over three millennia, and the city has been a capital under five dynasties.

funFacts.title: THE BIRD'S NEST
funFacts.text: The lattice-steel National Stadium, nicknamed the Bird's Nest, held the opening ceremonies of both Olympic Games.
